title: Meet C++ Checkpoint
intro: You have met the compiler, written a main function, printed text and read your first error messages. Eleven rounds, one from every idea in this module. Get them right first time to earn three stars!

rounds.prompt: Run this program. What appears on the screen?
options: Nothing: it needs a second endl
rounds.explain: `cout` prints whatever is inside the double quotes. The quotes mark where the text starts and ends, so they are not printed themselves.

rounds.prompt: Where does a C++ program start running?
options: At the first line of the file
rounds.explain: Every program begins at `main`. Misspell it and the build fails, because nothing tells the computer where to begin.

rounds.prompt: This line will not compile. Pick the fix.
options: Add a semicolon: cout << "Almost there" << endl;
Put the whole line in curly braces
rounds.explain: Every C++ instruction ends with a semicolon. Without it `g++` keeps reading onto the next line and reports `expected ';'`.

options: Brings in the standard tools for printing, such as `cout`
rounds.explain: The preprocessor pastes in the declarations of the input and output tools. Without it the compiler has never heard of `cout`. Skipping `std::` is the job of `using namespace std;`.

rounds.prompt: Careful: only one of these ends the line. What is the output?
rounds.explain: The first `cout` has no `endl`, so `Lab` continues straight after `Pocket` with no space. Only the `endl` ends the line.

options: Nothing: you cannot print a number after text
rounds.explain: `<<` sends each piece to the screen in turn. Text comes out as written, and the number 10 is printed as the digits 1 and 0.

rounds.prompt: Which escape sequence prints a double quote?
rounds.explain: `\n` is a new line, `\t` is a tab and `\\` is a single backslash. `\"` prints a double quote without ending the text.

rounds.prompt: This program compiles and prints nothing at all. Why?
options: The `//` turned the instruction into a comment, so it is ignored
rounds.explain: Anything after `//` is a note for humans. Commenting out a line switches it off without deleting it, which is a handy way to test what a line was doing.

rounds.prompt: Your program prints two lines and then stops without finishing. What kind of error is it?
options: A compile error: `g++` refused to build it
Both a compile and a runtime error
Not an error: programs always print two lines first
A runtime error: it compiled, started, then broke
rounds.explain: Output appearing proves the code compiled and started running, so whatever went wrong happened while the program was running.

rounds.prompt: Match each piece of C++ to what it does.

pairs.right: Checks your code and builds an executable
Marks the end of an instruction
Starts a note the compiler ignores

rounds.explain: These six cover the whole module: building your code, bringing in tools, the starting point, printing, and the two bits of punctuation you will type most often.

rounds.prompt: Build the smallest working program: include the printing tools, use the std names, open main, print a greeting, report success, then close main.
rounds.explain: The setup lines come first so the compiler knows about `cout` before `main` uses it. Inside `main` the greeting is printed, `return 0;` reports success, and the brace closes `main`.
